https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/the-aws.title: The AWS MCP Server is now generally available
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/the-aws.summary: AWS has announced the general availability of the AWS MCP Server, a managed implementation of the Model Context Protocol designed to provide AI agents and coding assistants with secure, real-time access to AWS services. The server addresses common limitations of AI models—such as outdated training data and inefficient command usage—by offering tools for live API execution, documentation retrieval, and sandboxed script execution, all while maintaining enterprise-grade security and auditability.
key_points: The AWS MCP Server allows AI agents to execute over 15,000 AWS API operations using existing IAM credentials and SigV4 authentication.
A new 'Skills' feature replaces standard operating procedures with curated, service-team-maintained guidance to ensure agents build production-ready infrastructure.
The 'run_script' tool enables server-side execution of Python scripts in a sandboxed environment, reducing token consumption and latency by chaining multiple API calls.
Enterprise security is prioritized through IAM context keys, Service Control Policies (SCPs), and dedicated CloudWatch metrics to distinguish agent activity from human actions.
Real-time documentation access allows AI agents to support newly released services that exist beyond their model's training knowledge cutoff.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/the-aws.why_it_matters: This release is a significant step in maturing AI-driven DevOps. By providing a secure bridge between LLMs and cloud infrastructure, AWS is enabling businesses to move from experimental AI chatbots to production-capable AI agents that can accurately and safely manage cloud resources, reducing the risk of security misconfigurations and technical debt.

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/moderni.title: Modernize your workflows: Amazon WorkSpaces now gives AI agents their own desktop (preview)
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/moderni.summary: Amazon WorkSpaces has launched a preview feature that enables AI agents to operate desktop and legacy applications directly within managed virtual desktops. This innovation allows enterprises to automate workflows within systems that lack modern APIs by giving AI agents their own secure desktop environment where they can interact with software via computer vision and simulated inputs.
key_points: Addresses the 'API gap' for the 75% of organizations running legacy applications that currently lack programmatic access.
Utilizes 'Computer vision' for screen capture and 'Computer input' for clicking and typing, allowing agents to use software exactly like human employees.
Built-in enterprise governance through AWS IAM for authentication and AWS CloudTrail for comprehensive audit trails of agent activities.
Supports the industry-standard Model Context Protocol (MCP), making it compatible with frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, and Strands Agents.
Currently available in public preview across major AWS regions, including US East, US West, Europe, and Asia.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/moderni.why_it_matters: This technology bypasses the traditional requirement for expensive and time-consuming application modernization. For businesses with legacy or mainframe-dependent processes, it provides a fast-track to AI adoption, allowing them to scale productivity and automate complex workflows without rewriting their existing software infrastructure.

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-wee.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: What’s Next with AWS 2026, Amazon Quick, OpenAI partnership, and more (May 4, 2026)
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-wee.summary: AWS has announced a major strategic expansion centered on 'agentic AI' and a deepened partnership with OpenAI. Key highlights include the integration of GPT-5 series models into Amazon Bedrock, the transformation of Amazon Quick into a comprehensive AI workplace assistant, and the verticalization of Amazon Connect into four specialized agentic solutions for supply chain, healthcare, recruitment, and customer service.
key_points: AWS and OpenAI expanded their partnership to bring GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, and the Codex coding agent to Amazon Bedrock in limited preview.
Amazon Quick evolved into a cross-platform AI assistant with a new desktop app, visual asset generation, and natural-language app building capabilities.
Amazon Connect is now a suite of four agentic solutions: Decisions (supply chain), Talent (AI-led hiring), Customer (CX), and Health (clinical documentation).
Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents now leverage OpenAI frontier models for enhanced reasoning and reliable steering of complex business tasks.
New 8th-generation EC2 instances (M8, R8, and C8) powered by 6th-gen Intel Xeon processors and Nitro cards offer up to 43% higher performance.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-wee.why_it_matters: This shift indicates that AWS is moving beyond basic cloud infrastructure to provide specialized, industry-specific AI agents. By integrating OpenAI's most advanced frontier models with enterprise-grade security and governance in Bedrock, AWS is positioning itself as the primary hub for production-ready generative AI, while simultaneously challenging SaaS productivity leaders through the expanded capabilities of Amazon Quick.

https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/r.title: Red Hat Summit 2026: Platform modernization and AI on Microsoft Azure Red Hat OpenShift
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/r.summary: At the Red Hat Summit 2026, Microsoft and Red Hat showcased Microsoft Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) as a critical platform for enterprise-scale AI and application modernization. Microsoft was recognized with the Red Hat Ecosystem Innovation Award for Platform Modernization. ARO helps organizations transition AI projects from pilot to production with consistent governance, security, and scalability, as demonstrated by customers like Banco Bradesco and Topicus. The platform offers advancements in modernization, security (including Zero Trust, Confidential Containers, and Managed Identities), AI innovation (with expanded NVIDIA GPU support), and global expansion, providing a jointly engineered, enterprise-ready foundation for critical workloads.
key_points: Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) is positioned as an enterprise-grade platform supporting production AI workloads and comprehensive application modernization efforts.

Microsoft received the 2026 Red Hat Ecosystem Innovation Award for Platform Modernization, highlighting successful customer outcomes like Banco Bradesco's 200+ AI initiatives and Topicus's regulated lending platform built on ARO.

ARO features advanced security capabilities, including a Zero Trust approach, Confidential Containers for data-in-use protection, and Managed/Workload Identities for secure credential management, crucial for regulated industries.

The platform offers flexibility for AI innovation, allowing customers to run AI directly with Red Hat OpenShift AI or integrate with Azure AI services, supported by expanded NVIDIA GPU capabilities for data-intensive workloads.

OpenShift Virtualization on ARO provides a practical path for enterprises to migrate legacy virtual machines alongside containers on a single managed platform, simplifying licensing and offering a phased modernization strategy.
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/r.why_it_matters: For businesses, Azure Red Hat OpenShift provides a strategic advantage by offering a secure, scalable, and jointly supported platform to operationalize AI initiatives and modernize IT infrastructure. It addresses key challenges such as moving AI from experimentation to production, ensuring consistent governance and security across hybrid environments, and meeting strict regulatory and data sovereignty requirements. This enables organizations to accelerate digital transformation, reduce operational overhead, and maintain compliance while leveraging cutting-edge AI capabilities.

https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/b.title: Build AI apps with Azure Cosmos DB: Key trends from Cosmos Conf 2026
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/b.summary: The Cosmos Conf 2026 highlighted that AI is fundamentally reshaping application and data platform architectures, moving beyond just another workload. Key trends include the shift towards flexible, semi-structured data for AI applications, a dramatic acceleration in development pace driven by AI and coding agents, and the emergence of semantic search as a first-class query operator. Customer examples from OpenAI, Vercel, and Walmart demonstrated the critical need for databases that offer extreme scalability, schema flexibility, serverless operations, global distribution, real-time performance, and built-in cost efficiency to support AI-native applications.
key_points: AI is making flexible, semi-structured data foundational for applications, shifting databases from systems of record to systems of reasoning.
AI and coding agents are accelerating development, requiring databases to support rapid iteration, instant scalability, serverless form factors, and agent-friendly interfaces.
Semantic search (vector, full-text, hybrid, semantic ranking) is now a core requirement for AI applications, necessitating integrated retrieval, reasoning, and real-time context.

Leading organizations (OpenAI, Vercel, Walmart) are building AI-native applications that demand instant scalability from zero to massive usage, schema-less design, serverless architectures, global distribution, and high reliability.
Cost efficiency is becoming a core design principle, requiring real-time cost visibility for developers and upfront architectural design for efficiency.
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/b.why_it_matters: This article is critical for businesses as it outlines the fundamental shifts AI is driving in application development and data infrastructure. To remain competitive, businesses must adapt their data strategies to accommodate flexible, semi-structured data, embrace serverless architectures, empower developers with tools that accelerate iteration, and integrate advanced semantic search capabilities. Investing in globally distributed, highly scalable, and cost-efficient data platforms like Azure Cosmos DB is essential to build and maintain the next generation of AI-powered applications while ensuring performance, reliability, and developer productivity.

https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/s.title: Scaling cloud and AI: Microsoft Azure’s commitment to Europe’s digital future
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/s.summary: Microsoft Azure is making significant strategic investments in its cloud and AI infrastructure across Europe, expanding datacenter regions and capacity to meet rapidly accelerating customer demand. These investments are designed to provide trusted, sovereign cloud solutions that ensure data residency, operational control, and compliance with local regulations, enabling European organizations to scale their AI and digital transformation initiatives.
key_points: Microsoft is heavily investing in expanding its Azure datacenter regions and capacity across Northern and Southern Europe to support growing cloud and AI demand.
The focus is on providing 'sovereign solutions' that offer transparency, operational control, and adherence to local and EU data residency and compliance requirements.

European public sector entities and enterprises are leveraging Azure and Azure OpenAI for diverse applications, from streamlining operations (Manchester City Council) to product information management (Inriver) and manufacturing (Sandvik).

Examples from Northern Europe (e.g., Sweden, Denmark) highlight sustainable datacenter designs and AI innovation, while Southern Europe (e.g., Spain, Italy, Greece) showcases accelerated digital transformation and low-latency critical workloads.

The investments enable organizations to deploy cloud and AI services locally, ensuring proximity to users, strong digital resilience, and compliance with national and EU regulations without compromising access to advanced capabilities.
https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/s.why_it_matters: This initiative underscores Microsoft's commitment to powering Europe's digital future and AI adoption. For businesses, it translates to enhanced access to scalable, secure, and compliant cloud and AI infrastructure within Europe, offering greater choice for data residency, improved performance, and critical tools to accelerate innovation, meet regulatory demands, and drive digital transformation across various industries.
